_readme: insta-studio's own notes on every style, kept apart from the upstream style.json files so a library update never overwrites them. renderer: svg = draw with the React/SVG kit; canvas = port the drawing into <StyleCanvas> (2D canvas); three = <StyleCanvas> with three.js (WebGL). material: none = everything can be drawn in code; real = the style is built on real footage, photos, scans or survey data, so it only fits a reel when the owner supplies that material and has the rights to it. note: what to watch for on a 9:16 narrated reel. Regenerate styles/README.md with: node scripts/styles-index.mjs

storybook.note: The house style. Uses the kit as is.

art-deco.note: Keep the centre axis vertical on 9:16.

ascii-crt.note: Size the character grid for 1080 wide so text stays readable on a phone.

backrooms.note: Eerie by design. Check it suits the account's tone.

brick-toy.note: Generic studded bricks only, never a toy brand's look or minifigures.

briefing-board.note: Needs real cut-out photographs of the subject.

caption-news.note: Needs real footage, photos or documents. Its huge captions replace our subtitles, and keep them inside the safe zones.

cel-anime-80s.note: Original characters only. Draw the mascot as a cel.

chalkboard.note: Good for 'what people think vs what is true' hooks.

circuit-board.note: Good for flows: money, power, data.

countdown.note: Needs real footage of one event with a known zero.

crayon-book.note: Closest to the house style. Easy first try.

dark-keynote.note: Product or app explainers. One giant number per beat.

data-physical.note: Real statistics built as objects: every number sourced, as BRAND.md asks anyway.

dataviz.note: Real data, sourced and dated. Strong fit for number-led explainers.

desktop-flythrough.note: Draw generic app cards, never a real app's logo or UI.

glass-product.note: Needs a GPU for a fast render. Generic products only.

halftone-dossier.note: Good for 'the case of…' and myth-busting reels.

hd-2d.note: Pixel sprites in a lit 3D diorama. Draw the mascot as a sprite.

iso-infographic.note: Strong fit for 'how a system works' explainers.

isometric-picture-book.note: Faceless people seen from behind; the mascot can be the one character with a face.

kino-montage.note: Needs real archive footage and photos.

lidar-survey.note: Needs a real laser-scan point cloud.

living-screencast.note: Draw a generic interface, never a real product's UI.

microgame.note: Each microgame switches art style; keep the mascot the same in all of them.

news-package.note: All graphics drawn in code. Its lower-third strap must clear the bottom safe zone.

one-line.note: Redraw the mascot as one continuous line.

pictogram-motion.note: Beat-locked: time the cuts to the music grid.

pixel-rpg.note: Draw at 180×320 and scale up with nearest-neighbour. Original sprites only.

printed-long-take.note: One unbroken camera move: plan the whole route before drawing.

rubber-hose.note: Original characters only. Jazz music style.

satellite-briefing.note: Needs real satellite imagery with a licence that allows reuse.

silent-film.note: Its intertitles replace a narrator: keep our narration and use intertitles as the subtitles. The 4:3 print sits inside 9:16 between curtains.

silkscreen-poster.note: Good for covers and carousels too.

swiss-motion.note: No characters by nature: the mascot can appear as one geometric shape, or skip it.

teardown.note: Needs the product's real engineering files.

telestrator.note: Needs real match footage with reuse rights.

tilt-shift.note: Built in 3D, so no real photos are needed.

visual-investigation.note: Needs real footage, documents and audio from one event.

white-model.note: Needs real building and map data for the place.
